summary: Fixed a live reopen-after-broker-stop race in S007: decide() could still want a label the broker had already stopped out (its own M1-bar plan lagged the real tick-based fill by one cycle) and would attempt to re-place it with a now-invalid stop, saved only by luck when the broker rejected the order (TRADING_BAD_STOPS). Added StrategyLogger.label_was_opened() and made decide() backfill the close (reason=broker_side_close_detected) the same cycle it notices a previously-opened label missing from broker positions, instead of waiting for the next cycle to notice. Added regression tests covering both the new label_was_opened() method and the end-to-end decide() path.

Extracted the S007 decide()/reconcile logic out of bot/s007_paper.py::live() into a reusable run_cycle_for_account(creds, preset, risk_pct, fixed_lot, use_fixed_lot, magic, logger, ...) function, parameterized instead of hardcoded to bot.s007_config globals; live() now just calls it with the module defaults, so the single-account CLI behaviour is unchanged (verified via --dry-run regression). Rewrote webapp/runner.py for the new broker-agnostic multi-strategy schema (User/Account/AccountStrategy/Strategy) as a coordinator+worker pair: "python -m webapp.runner --strategy S007" loads enabled AccountStrategy rows and spawns one worker subprocess per account (because CTraderAdapter drives its session through a single reactor.run() call -- Twisted reactors cannot be restarted in the same process, so parallel accounts within one tick require one OS process each, not threads/asyncio); a worker runs exactly one cycle for one account_strategy id and exits. Curated events (cycle_start/cycle_end/position_open/position_close/error) now also write to the DB logs table via webapp/schemas/logs.py; full per-tick debug detail (and the label_was_opened/closed dedup state decide() depends on) still goes to per-account utils.trade_logger.StrategyLogger JSONL files under reports/logs/ -- NOT yet safe to drop for containerization, since that dedup state currently only lives in those files (open item). Rewrote webapp/cli.py for the same new schema (init-db/create-user/add-account/add-strategy/link-strategy/enable/disable/list), reusing webapp/schemas/ for validation. S009/Bybit multi-account support deliberately NOT done here: bot/s009_paper.py keeps its ledger state in one shared file for the whole strategy (load_state/save_state), not per (account, strategy), so it would need its own refactor before it could run several accounts in parallel the same way.

Tested the new webapp.runner (coordinator+worker subprocess-per-account) end to end against the real DB-migrated S007/CTRADER account: coordinator found 1 enabled account_strategy row, spawned a worker, worker decrypted DB credentials, ran a full cTrader reconcile cycle, and wrote cycle_start/cycle_end to both the file logger and the DB logs table; account_strategies.status/last_cycle_at updated correctly. Uninstalled the old single-account launchd job (com.anton.algo.s007bot) now that the DB-driven runner path works. Two initial worker runs appeared to hang (55s+ with no output) -- root-caused to stdout full-buffering in a non-TTY subprocess hiding progress, combined with what looks like transient cTrader demo-server slowness, not a code bug: two subsequent clean runs completed in ~7s, matching the old single-account path.

Load-tested the multi-account parallel fan-out with two throwaway benchmark scripts (not committed): (1) N mocked no-network workers (Python startup + one DB query each) scale well -- N=40 parallel finishes in ~1.8s wall time, so coordinator/DB overhead is not the bottleneck. (2) N real concurrent cTrader demo-server sessions against the SAME account/client_id: N=5 all succeed in ~4.2s; N=10 mostly succeed at ~4.6s but one session stalled to 36.8s; N=15 failed to complete within 90s (at least one session hung indefinitely). This points at the cTrader DEMO server itself, not our code, as the scaling limit for near-simultaneous sessions on one account/client_id -- unclear if this generalizes to N DIFFERENT accounts/client_ids in production (untested, no second real account available). Suggests staggering worker starts and/or adding retry-with-backoff in run_worker() before scaling account count up.

Follow-up load test isolating our own fan-out/DB overhead from the cTrader demo-server bottleneck found in the previous test: a throwaway mock worker (sleeps a fixed 5s to simulate broker latency, then does the same DB read+write pattern run_worker() does against the real sqlite DB, no real network) scales cleanly -- N=20/50/100/200 parallel workers all succeed with wall times of 5.7s/7.0s/8.9s/14.1s and no outlier tail latency (max per-worker ~9s even at N=200). Confirms the coordinator/subprocess-fan-out/SQLite-write design is NOT the bottleneck for scaling account count; the earlier-found slowdown (some sessions stalling to 30s+ at N=10 real broker connections) is specific to the cTrader demo server handling concurrent sessions on one account/client_id, not our architecture. Still unverified: whether that broker-side limit is per-account, per-client_id, or per-IP -- matters for whether it actually constrains production (different users -> different client_ids). Needs testing with a second real distinct account once available.

Surfaced S007 "ghost" trades: plan_now() now returns reached_tp/n_recovery in context and a new resolved list of positions the engine entered AND resolved (stop/tp/daycap) within the same replayed bars -- these never reach the broker because decide() only places orders for still-open ('eod') positions, so previously they left no trace at all. decide() now logs each first-seen resolved position via a new StrategyLogger.label_was_ghosted()-guarded position(label, "ghost", ...) call. Investigated live 2026-08-05: a B setup formed and resolved before any cycle saw it as open; a historical replay of the events log (2026-08-01 through 2026-08-05) found 2 prior days (08-01, 08-03) with the same pattern -- a scenario detected, n_desired never above 0, no order ever placed -- newly distinguishable from a normal no-signal day now that this is logged.

Fixed a live order-placement bug found while checking today's S007 logs: every cycle since 10:03 today (2026-08-06) rejected with INVALID_REQUEST "Order price ... has more digits than symbol allows" (e.g. 26081.200000000004 for a DE40 symbol that only accepts 2 decimals) -- sl_price/tp_price flow through several float ops (range mid, swing stops) on quotes with up to 5 decimals (PRICE_SCALE), so an unrounded value routinely picks up float noise past the symbol precision. _place_market_step now rounds both to full_symbol.digits (already fetched per cycle for sizing) before sending. No dedicated regression test added yet -- would need the fake-SDK harness in tests/bot/test_check_response.py, which currently fails at collection for an unrelated reason (ctrader_s007 import error), not investigated further here.

Fixed two problems in this test file found while checking today's trading logs. (1) Its autouse _clean_position_log fixture was shutil.rmtree()-ing the REAL reports/logs/S007/positions/ directory before/after every test (not a tmp dir) -- running this file while the live launchd tick (com.anton.algo.s007bot) happened to be mid-cycle deleted all production per-position history and threw a FileNotFoundError in that live cycle (incident 2026-08-06, see decisions-log.md; no data was actually lost, since every position/order event is duplicated into reports/logs/S007/events-<date>.jsonl, untouched by this). Replaced it with monkeypatch.setattr(s007_paper, 'LOG', StrategyLogger("S007TEST", log_root=str(tmp_path))) -- same per-test isolation guarantee, zero risk to real data. (2) The 4 tests mocking plan_now via lambda m1: ... had been broken (TypeError: unexpected keyword argument preset) since the 2026-07-31 run_cycle_for_account refactor added preset=preset to the real call site without updating these mocks; widened the lambda signature to lambda m1, preset=None: .... All 17 tests in the file (plus test_s007_signals.py and test_label_was_closed.py) pass now.

Fixed a second live order-placement bug found today (2026-08-06), right after the price-rounding one: a b-reversal leg is simulated against its own target (tp_A, the opposite range boundary) via _simulate_leg(...tp_A...), but engine.py never stored that per-leg tp on the position dict, and s007_signals.py::plan_now built every wanted positions tp from the single day-level r["tp"] (the PRIMARY B legs target). Live: a reversal BUY went out with the original SELL legs (lower) target attached and cTrader rejected it outright (TRADING_BAD_STOPS: New TP for BUY pending order should be > entry price), repeating every cycle for labels :93/:114/:117 from 11:38 onward, following the same pattern as the earlier :1/:13/:38 sequence. Fix: _simulate_leg now stores tp=tp on every position dict it creates (both the initial entry and pyramided adds); plan_now uses each positions own p["tp"] instead of the shared day-level tp when building wanted/resolved. Verified against the real 2026-06-17 B-stopped/A-reversal-hit-tp historical day (same one used for the ghost-trade fix): the still-open reversal leg now reports tp=24818.666 (rl, correct) instead of 25110.899 (the primary legs tp, which was invalid on the reversal sellside too). Added a regression test asserting a wanted positions tp differs from the day-level context tp and is on the correct side of its own entry.

Added a day-done short-circuit to webapp/runner.py's DB-driven S007 worker: unlike the legacy scripts/s007_tick.py (loop_settled/loop_resumed guard), _worker_s007 used to open a real cTrader/Twisted session on every dispatcher tick for the rest of the session window even after the day's target was already reached. Fixed by stamping link.status = 'settled:<local date>' once a cycle comes back day_done/filtered/manual_stop, and returning immediately -- before constructing any creds/logger/broker session -- on a later same-day tick. Self-resetting: a new day's first tick has a stale date in status and runs normally, no separate reset needed. Also refreshed webapp/README.md (mostly already current from other work; added sections on the STRATEGY_WORKERS registry, S009's shadow-only DB-driven state, and the deployment/schedule.yml + scripts/scheduler_tick.py + Docker/Ofelia scheduling layer, none of which were documented there yet) and confirmed the empty _to_delete/ directory is already gone (git doesn't track empty dirs).

Fixed two real bugs found live during S007 first trading day on the new Docker/Ofelia path: (1) dispatch job-run container ran in UTC instead of Europe/Kyiv (missing TZ env on the label), causing S007 to silently skip its 10:00-13:00 Kyiv session window; (2) scheduler_tick had no overlap guard, so a slow cycle (55-118s, observed live) let two dispatch ticks run the same strategy concurrently -- added a per-(kind,name) file lock under data/.scheduler_locks with stale-lock self-healing. Also fixed podman_healthcheck.py: the watchdog previously treated a fully-unreachable (stopped) machine as non-healable and did nothing, leaving zero dispatch coverage for 25+ minutes live during an open real position; now both drift and unreachable trigger the same heal path, and each heal step is wrapped so a failing subprocess call cannot crash the healthcheck itself. Root cause of the recurring Podman-machine instability (3 outages in ~2.5h today) remains unexplained -- watchdog now reacts correctly to all observed failure modes but does not fix why the VM keeps dying.

Fully deactivated the legacy launchd path for S007 (Trello: "Развести Ofelia и launchd-агент com.anton.algo.s007bot", Tier-1). Removed the installed plist from ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ (was already unloaded since the 2026-08-09 Docker cutover, but still one launchctl load away from an accident -- both paths independently manage the same demo account ctrader-47939312). Added explicit DEPRECATED headers to scripts/s007_tick.py and the tracked scripts/com.anton.algo.s007bot.plist explaining the manual break-glass recovery procedure (docker compose down ofelia FIRST, then reinstall+load), and updated docker-compose.yml comment accordingly. No code logic changed, only docs/comments + removing the installed artifact; 51 tests still pass.

Fixed a live S007 regression: commit f9e8fdd (this session, committing pre-existing uncommitted work) had silently dropped tp=tp from both position-dict constructors in engine.py::_simulate_leg. Harmless for the PRIMARY leg (its own tp param equals the p.get("tp", tp) fallback s007_signals.py already uses), but it broke the b_reversal_to_A recovery leg: simulated with tp_A (the OPPOSITE-direction target) but never storing it on its own positions, so the fallback silently substituted the PRIMARY leg tp instead. Live effect, caught while running trading-analysis on S007 today: cTrader rejected every recovery-leg order for ~27 minutes straight (10:19-10:44 Kyiv) with TRADING_BAD_STOPS (New TP for SELL pending order should be < entry price), until the setups aged out and resolved as -1R stop-loss ghosts without ever reaching the broker (no real fill/loss, but 4 legitimate recovery-leg trading opportunities were missed). Restored tp=tp on both position dicts. Added tests/strategies/ger40_lonfra/test_engine.py exercising the REAL _simulate_leg/simulate_day (existing tests/bot/test_s007_signals.py coverage mocks simulate_day entirely, so it never caught this) -- verified both new tests fail against the pre-fix code and pass after. Separately (infra, not logged to a strategy component): found and fixed the Podman machine flapping unreachable every ~5min since 08:52 today (host swap at 94%, 16.4GB/17.4GB used) via a manual machine stop/start, which is what let this cycle actually run and surface the bug.

Fixed _auth_account() and _load_symbols() silently swallowing ProtoOAErrorRes account-auth rejections as opaque AttributeErrors instead of raising the real broker error. Found live 2026-08-17: S007 cycles failed from session start with a masked "Trading account is not authorized" error; the real cause was CH_ACCESS_TOKEN_INVALID (expired cTrader access token) -- needs a fresh token in configs/accounts.yml, no code fix restores trading by itself.

Added scripts/ctrader_oauth.py to mint a fresh cTrader access token via the OAuth2 authorization-code flow (id.ctrader.com authorize + openapi.ctrader.com/apps/token GET exchange, per the official docs) for when the stored one expires. Used live 2026-08-17 to recover S007 after CH_ACCESS_TOKEN_INVALID: new token written into configs/accounts.yml AND into the Account row credentials in data/app.db (webapp/runner.py sources cTrader creds from the DB, not accounts.yml, for the live Docker path) -- both needed updating, accounts.yml alone would not have fixed the live scheduler.

Added NEWS_SAFE_EXIT_END='14:24' and preset WORKING_S007_NEWSSAFE (= WORKING_S007_LIQFLOOR with the day flattened at 14:24 instead of 16:59) as the prop-firm deployment candidate, after a per-minute M1 volatility study showed the 15:30 Kyiv bar (US 8:30 ET releases) has a p99 of 50.6 bps against a ~3 bps all-day median, with the ECB decision at 15:15 just ahead of it. Backtest 2023-06-26..2026-08-11 on both cost models ACCEPTED it: bps net +0.8498 -> +0.9161 R/day, win 60 -> 62%, worst day unchanged at -8.69R, weakest year 2023 +18.0 -> +43.9R; only 2025 gives ground. exit_end is a plateau (14:29..15:29 = 97-105% of the 16:59 result), so the cutoff was chosen on the a-priori scheduled-release ground rather than by picking the best number. Base presets and the engine untouched; REF_* regression presets re-run and unchanged. Also corrected the now-stale WORKING_S007_LIQFLOOR comment, which still said 'backtest NOT YET RUN, do not promote' although it was validated and promoted to live on 2026-08-12.

Documentation audit and Confluence migration: moved the S004 passport + E0-E11 experiments log (docs/STRATEGY_S004.md, docs/EXPERIMENTS.md) and the gap-fade research handoff (docs/HANDOFF_GAP_FADE_RESEARCH.md, previously untracked) to Confluence pages under Strategies (ids 10944530, 11042817), leaving English pointer stubs in the repo. Fixed stale claims: README live preset WORKING_S007 -> WORKING_S007_LIQFLOOR and outdated "S007 backtests not mirrored" note, expanded runner/docs lists; bot/S007_README.md preset BASELINE_S007 -> WORKING_S007_LIQFLOOR; deployment/schedule.yml and scripts/fetch_deribit_snapshot.py comments "S012 candidate" -> S013 (Deribit strangle was renumbered when S012 went to cross-sectional momentum). Confluence Strategies page updated to v7 (S004 link + pre-registry candidates section). Known drift left for consent: .claude/skills/strategy-lifecycle/SKILL.md line 56 still names the moved docs as live.

Documented (no behavior change) a live incident 2026-08-31 10:03 Kyiv: a B-down setup live order used entry=26440.6 (from the M1 bar closed only 4s earlier) with tp=26442.6, rejected by cTrader (TRADING_BAD_STOPS: TP must be < entry on a SELL). The 10:05 cycle re-scanned with 2 more bars and resolved the same setup already-tp'd at a different bar (entry=26469.1), consistent with the freshly-closed bar not having fully settled broker-side at query time. Unlike bot/s009_paper.py's drop_forming, nothing in run_live_cycle/find_setup excludes the most-recently-closed M1 bar. Not a regression of the 2026-08-06 (wrong per-leg tp) or 2026-08-13 (missing tp=tp on recovery leg) bugs -- both n_recovery=0 and the day-level tp were correct here. Even a fix likely would not have caught this specific trade live: by 10:05 the whole entry->TP move had already happened within already-elapsed bars, same class as the ghost-trade/1-minute-poll limitation behind promoting WORKING_S007_LIQFLOOR (decisions-log.md 2026-08-11/12). Added an in-code comment at the M1 fetch site in run_live_cycle recording this; no fix applied -- touching find_setup's bar window is a signal-engine behavior change needing backtest validation (Gate 0/1) first, and even so may not change the practical outcome. Anton chose to document only, not file a ticket or change behavior, this session.

ALGODEV-14 (meta-labeling over S007): applied the S004 meta-labeling methodology to S007 with three new scripts (backtest/s007_metalabel_data.py dataset builder, s007_metalabel_gate0.py no-look-ahead check, s007_metalabel_eval.py evaluation). Unit-of-learning decision: the DAY, not the individual add -- quantified on the engine's actual position lists (92% of traded days pyramid, 2233 adds, 79% share the first position's exit status via the common mid_range stop / day TP), so per-add labels would be pseudo-replicates; daily R aggregation preserved for passport comparability. Dataset: 680 traded days 2023-06-26..2026-08-11, 14 causal entry-time features (scenario/direction/height_bps/entry_minute/first_risk_frac/dist_to_tp_R/entry_pos_in_range/gap/asia range/prev-day ATR%/trend/dow), regression-verified (net +0.8008 R/day LIQFLOOR, +0.8665 NEWSSAFE at 0.635pt/side, byte-matching the 2026-08-21 passport numbers); Gate 0 PASSED (truncate at 2025-06-01, max|delta|=0 on all features). Evaluation: expanding yearly walk-forward (train<Y, test=Y, threshold chosen on train only), logit + small GBM, expectancy- and drawdown-targeted thresholds, on BOTH presets. VERDICT: FAIL -- every configuration skips days that are on average PROFITABLE (+0.66..+1.10 R/day skipped), total R always drops (LIQFLOOR logit/net +539.7R -> +435.0R stitched OOS), maxDD barely improves (-37.4 -> -36.7R) or worsens (NEWSSAFE logit/net -29.3 -> -42.1R); best DD-targeted cut (-37.4 -> -32.2R) costs -111R; worst day untouched (-8.87 -> -8.56R). The ticket's separate drawdown question is answered NO: the martingale-like DD comes from the intraday add path on chop days, which entry-time features do not predict. No engine/config change, no flag added; verdict recorded in s007_metalabel_eval.py docstring. Scripts left untracked like the S004 metalabel precedent.

ALGODEV-14 follow-up (worst-day tail study): found that ALL 30 worst days (<=-5R) on WORKING_S007_LIQFLOOR are B 'double failures' (primary leg fully stopped, then the b_reversal_to_A recovery leg fully stopped too; 28/30 have exactly 8 positions). The pattern is NOT predictable: not by entry-time features (the meta-labeling FAIL), not at the flip moment (187 recovery legs, corr ~0 with flip time / realized damage / height), not by calendar (weekday flat, 0/30 on NFP or opex Fridays, 15:30-bar release proxy flat; the April-2024 cluster is one bad regime month), not by Asia/PDH-PDL liquidity geometry, and not by HTF context (counter-H1 days carry 2x tail rate at the SAME +0.75 expectancy). Two mechanical modifiers therefore tested via backtest/run_s007_tailrisk.py (pre-declared: cap=2, H1 SMA50, weight 0.5; Gate 0 on the H1 flag passed): (1) HTF half-risk on counter-H1 days REJECTED -- cuts profit more than drawdown (-18.5% sum for -15.3% maxDD), dominated by uniform size-scaling; (2) NEW ENGINE FLAG max_recovery_positions (default None = base untouched; regression: REF_PYRAMID_LIQ_DUKA + both working presets byte-identical with flag off) at cap=2 ACCEPTED for the prop worst-day axis only: -6.1..-6.7% profit for -25% worst day (-9.03 -> -6.75R), maxDD ~unchanged, all years positive on NEWSSAFE (2023 +24.6R) though 2023 dips to -0.8R on LIQFLOOR. Added preset WORKING_S007_PROP = WORKING_S007_NEWSSAFE.with_(max_recovery_positions=2), explicitly NOT promoted to any bot config -- candidate pending Anton's decision; note it fixes only the DAILY-limit axis, not max total drawdown. Verdicts recorded in config.py flag comment and run_s007_tailrisk.py docstring.

ALGODEV-35: added liquidity_tp_ceiling_points (StrategyConfig) and wired it into engine.py::liquidity_tp -- caps a liquidity TP that lies beyond range_tp at range_tp+/-N points, on top of the existing liquidity_tp_floor (ALGODEV-21) which only stops a target being NEARER than range_tp. Prompted by a live 2026-09-02 case (Anton): a real S007 cycle picked liquidity 285.9pt beyond range_tp for its TP. Added 6 named presets (WORKING_S007_LIQCEIL10/20/30/40/50/100, all WORKING_S007_LIQFLOOR + a ceiling) and backtest/run_s007_liqceiling.py sweeping all 6 against uncapped LIQFLOOR at Gate 1 (gross) and Gate 2 (real spread 0.635/side) on the same 2026-08-11 Dukascopy refresh run_s007_liqfloor.py used -- confirmed a byte-matching regression against that script before trusting the new numbers. Verdict: REJECTED, all six. Gate 2 net R/day for ceil10..100 = +0.676/+0.687/+0.729/+0.784/+0.833/+0.837 vs uncapped LIQFLOORs +0.801 -- every ceiling <=40pt is worse (lower net, often deeper maxDD, e.g. ceil20/30 -65R vs -50.9R) despite a higher day win-rate (61-63% vs 60%); ceil50/100 approach uncapped but do not beat it (ceil100s maxDD is identical to uncapped, i.e. the cap essentially never binds there). Conclusion baked into the preset comments: distant liquidity targets that look alarming on any single day are net CONTRIBUTORS to the 3+-year edge, not noise -- capping them tighter loses profitability. WORKING_S007_LIQFLOOR (uncapped) stays the live preset; nothing promoted. default liquidity_tp_ceiling_points=None preserves byte-identical behavior for every existing preset (confirmed via the existing S007 test suite, 62 passed).

Day-scoped S007 risk caps after the 2026-09-02 incident (8 positions / ~-$401 / ~4% on a 2% cap day): both day caps in bot/s007_paper.py::decide were computed from the broker's open-positions snapshot, so every stop-out wave zeroed its own spent risk and the next wave got a fresh budget. Fix: (1) count cap now runs against opened_today_count -- every label our own append-only position log opened today (new StrategyLogger.open_records(prefix) in utils/trade_logger.py), union the live snapshot; (2) the $ gate now checks spent_risk_today = open_risk (broker fill/stop, unchanged) + closed-today risk at ACTUAL fill price, matched by position_id (now logged on the open record, extracted from ORDER_ACCEPTED) to the broker's last-24h closing deals -- run_live_cycle (bot/ctrader_s007.py) fetches _deal_list_step once per cycle in the same session and passes closed_deals into decide() (kwarg, default None -- old callers/fakes unaffected); planned-entry fallback when no deal matches, deal fetch failure falls back to [] and never kills the cycle. Slippage-inflated fills therefore keep counting at real size after closing. state/skip events now log spent_risk_today/closed_risk_today/opened_today. Replay of 2026-09-02's 8 opens vs the new gates: blocked from position 4 (10:57), day capped at ~-$194 spent of a $204 cap instead of -$401. Tests: 2 new in tests/bot/test_s007_live_sizing.py (stop-out waves; slipped fills from deal history incl. no-deals fallback); tests/bot/test_check_response.py SDK stub taught ProtoOADealListReq/ProtoOADealStatus (pre-existing breakage from the earlier deal-history import). Full run: 178 passed (tests/bot+utils+scripts+webapp).

ALGODEV-37 'maximally prop' scheme implemented AND cut over live (Anton's explicit decision: full switch, no parallel demo track). (1) New preset WORKING_S007_NEWSSAFE_MAX8_BE05 = NEWSSAFE_MAX8.with_(breakeven_at_r=0.5) -- verified dataclass-equal to run_s007_propscheme.py's winning ad-hoc combo (Gate 3: 100.0% cashout / 0.0% daily-bust). (2) Live breakeven: ProtoOAAmendPositionSLTPReq wired into bot/ctrader_s007.py (_amend_position_sltp_step, standalone amend_position_sl, 'amend' action kind in run_live_cycle using full_symbol.digits rounding). Trigger is the ENGINE's own be_moved flag surfaced through plan_now() (bot/s007_signals.py) -- same code path as the backtest, live/backtest can never disagree on WHEN; the amend targets the broker's ACTUAL fill price (have[lab]['price']) so real breakeven includes slippage; current takeProfit is always passed back because the amend message REPLACES both protection levels (unset TP would strip it). One-shot without extra state: decide() only amends when the current broker SL is strictly worse than the fill (buy: cur_sl<fill, sell: cur_sl>fill), so successful amends and manually-tightened stops are natural no-ops; failed amends retry next cycle. (3) FROZEN INVARIANT preserved (Anton: 'this must not break'): the 2026-09-02 day-cap fix untouched -- amends bypass opened_today/spent_risk_today accounting entirely, BE'd position still counts in the count cap; dedicated test. (4) webapp/runner.py taught the amend kind (previously everything non-open routed into _close_position_db -- an amend would have closed the DB row) + LogKind.POSITION_AMENDED. (5) Cutover: bot/s007_config.py PRESET -> WORKING_S007_NEWSSAFE_MAX8_BE05 AND EXIT_END '16:59' -> '14:24' -- CRITICAL PAIRING: plan_now() overrides the preset's session fields with s007_config values, a preset-only switch silently keeps trading to 16:59; DB (data/app.db): strategies.default_preset updated, link id=1 risk_pct 0.5 -> 0.25 (link currently enabled=0 -- re-enabling is Anton's call, NOT done this session); deployment/schedule.yml comment refreshed (cron window deliberately wider than EXIT_END). (6) Margin: new read-only scripts/check_s007_margin_8slots.py (ProtoOAExpectedMarginReq) run against the live demo -- 8 slots ~26.9% of balance, comfortable. FILL_PROB=0.75 confirmed ~0.735 empirically (prior session). Smoke: plan_now BE == engine BE on last 60 Dukascopy days (8/31 positions BE'd, all sl==entry; base preset never flags). Tests: 4 new in tests/bot/test_s007_live_breakeven.py; test_check_response SDK stub taught ProtoOAAmendPositionSLTPReq (fixes the 6 pre-existing errors); full run 149 passed. Docs: Jira ALGODEV-37 comment, Confluence S007 page 622593 v4 (status section) + work journal 10584066 v4, bot/S007_README.md.

ALGODEV-38: fixed a live bug where decide() could place a BRAND NEW S007 position with sl==entry (zero stop distance) -- found live 2026-09-03, recurred twice same session, second time also silently bypassing the day risk cap (new_risk computed from stop_distance collapsed to 0). Root cause: plan_now() replays the whole days bars every cycle, so a late-detected reversal/add leg can already show be_moved=True (engine moved p["stop"]=p["entry"] via its breakeven rule) on the very first cycle it appears as wanted, even though it was never actually open at the broker before -- decide()s place branch used that already-moved stop verbatim. Fix: bot/s007_signals.py::plan_now now also returns orig_sl per position (rederived from risk0, which the breakeven block never mutates); bot/s007_paper.py::decide()s place branch uses o.get("orig_sl", o["sl"]) instead of o["sl"] for both the risk-cap stop_distance calc and the placed orders sl. The existing amend path (ALGODEV-37) is unchanged -- it still moves the broker real stop to breakeven from the actual fill price once a position is genuinely open. ALGODEV-44 follow-up, MAJOR finding: added exit_idx to every simulated position (purely additive, feeds no R/cost calc, byte-identical regression confirmed) and a new backtest (run_s007_execution_realism.py) that excludes ghost trades -- positions whose exit_idx-idx <= 1, i.e. entered AND resolved within 1-2 M1 bars, which a 1-minute-polling live bot can never execute regardless of code speed (bot/s007_paper.py::decide places a newly eod position the same cycle it is first detected, and that cycle is already >=1 bar behind real time by construction). Result: ghosts are ~24-30% of ALL positions across every preset tested (including plain BASELINE_S007, not just b_reversal_to_A/BE stacks) and account for 80-88% of each presets total positive R. Live preset WORKING_S007_NEWSSAFE_MAX8_BE05 collapses from the previously-quoted +1.6513R/day (maxDD -19.2R, all years positive) to a REALISTIC +0.22-0.30R/day (maxDD -77 to -96R, at least one realistically-losing year) once ghosts are excluded. Triggered by a live-vs-backtest parity check on 5 real trading days (2026-09-10/11/14/15/16) that found the model would have netted +.87 on the same real bars while live actually netted -.02 -- live is UNDERPERFORMING even the sobered-up realistic number, meaning the earlier-found whipsaw/entry-slippage issues are additional, real problems layered on top of this validation-methodology gap, not an alternative explanation for it. This calls into question every previously-quoted net-R/day number for every S007 preset (BASELINE_S007 through the live preset), since none of the prior validation excluded ghost trades. Not yet documented in Jira/Confluence or reflected in config.py preset comments -- pending Antons direction.
